chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from his grandfather Al-Rabi' ibn Sa'd, who said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Rabi'! Indeed, a man may be truthful until Allah writes him as a truthful one (Siddiq).'

key_terms.صِدِّيقاً: A truthful one; a person of high rank in truthfulness, often associated with prophets and the righteous.
key_terms.يَصْدُقُ: He is truthful; practicing truthfulness in speech and deed.
key_terms.يَكْتُبَهُ اللَّهُ: Allah writes him; a metaphorical expression indicating divine recording of a person's status or character in the heavenly records.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of consistent truthfulness in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (as) illustrates the spiritual principle that habitual truthfulness (sidq) transforms into a fixed divine attribute, elevating the believer to the rank of 'Siddiq'. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that consistent practice (amal) solidifies character traits, aligning the individual with the prophetic tradition of truth as the foundation of faith. The narration underscores that honesty is not merely a moral virtue but a mechanism for spiritual certification by Allah.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Salim, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar Al Khazzaz, from his grandfather Al Rabie Bin Sa’ad who said,
‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Rabie! Let the man be truthful until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Writes him as a truthful one’.
en.sarwar: 8. Abu Ali al-Ash’ari has narrated from Muhammad ibn Salim from Ahmad ibn al- Nadr al-Khazzaz from his grandfather al-Rabi’ ibn Sa’d who has said the following: “Once
abu Ja’far (a.s.) said to me, ‘O Rab’i, a man must keep speaking the truth until Allah writes him down as a truthful one.’”
